lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext
- **Klassifikation:** UML-Klassendiagramm / AUTOSAR ECUC-Parametermetamodell-Fragment (BSW Parameter Configuration Metamodel).

- **Funktionale Einordnung:** Definiert die Konfigurationsstruktur des Containers `ComMUser` innerhalb des Communication Managers (`ComM`, System Services Layer, Classic AUTOSAR R4.0.3). Es modelliert die logischen Anforderer von Kommunikationsmodi (Software-Components via RTE, BswM, DCM) und deren Zuordnung zu Kommunikationskanälen sowie OS-Partitionen.
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
- **`ComMUser`** (`EcucParamConfContainerDef`):
- **Multiplizität:** `1..*` (Mindestens ein User muss pro ECU konfiguriert sein).
- Repräsentiert eine logische Nutzer-Entität, die Kommunikationsmodi (`COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION`, `COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION`, `COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION`) anfordert.
- **`ComMUserIdentifier`** (`EcucIntegerParamDef`):
- **Beziehung:** Komposition (`+parameter`) unter `ComMUser`.
- **Attribute:** `min = 0`, `max = 255`, `symbolicNameValue = true`.
- Eindeutige numerische ID des Nutzers (Kardinalität implizit 1..1, Datentyp `uint8` / `ComM_UserHandleType`). Dient der Generierung typsicherer symbolischer Header-Konstanten.
- **`ComMUserEcucPartitionRef`** (`EcucReferenceDef`):
- **Beziehung:** Komposition (`+reference`) unter `ComMUser`.
- **Multiplizität:** `0..1` (Optional).
- **Ziel (`+destination`):** Referenziert `EcucPartition` (`[0..*]` aus Package `EcucPartition`).
- Dient der Verankerung des Users in einer spezifischen Core-/Memory-Partition für Multicore- und Speicherschutz-Architekturen.
- **`ComMUserPerChannel`** (`EcucParamConfContainerDef`):
- **Multiplizität:** `0..*`.
- Sub-Container (üblicherweise unterhalb von `ComMChannel` angesiedelt), der die Zuordnung zwischen physischen/logischen Kanälen und Nutzern abbildet.
- **`ComMUserChannel`** (`EcucReferenceDef`):
- **Beziehung:** Komposition (`+reference`) unter `ComMUserPerChannel`.
- **Ziel (`+destination`):** Verweist zurück auf `ComMUser`.
- Schließt die M:N-Kanal-Nutzer-Relation: Ein Kanal verweist über diese Instanz auf die zugehörigen Nutzer, wodurch ein User gleichzeitig mehrere Kanäle steuern kann und umgekehrt.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
Als statisches ECUC-Metamodell-Diagramm bildet das Schaubild keinen sequenziellen Kontrollfluss ab; aus der Parameterstruktur resultiert jedoch folgende Laufzeitdynamik:
1. **Modusanforderung:** Ein Nutzer ruft synchron `ComM_RequestComMode(User, ComM_Mode)` auf. Die Zuordnung erfolgt über den aufgelösten `ComMUserIdentifier`.
2. **Kanalauflösung:** Der ComM ermittelt über die durch `ComMUserPerChannel` und `ComMUserChannel` generierten Lookup-Tabellen alle zugehörigen Kanäle (`ComMChannel`) bzw. Channel-Bitmasken.
3. **Zustandsaggregation:** Für alle referenzierten Kanäle wird die Modus-Schiedslogik (Mode Arbitration) durchlaufen; der höchste geforderte Kommunikationsmodus setzt sich durch.

4. **Partition-Boundary-Crossing:** Ist `ComMUserEcucPartitionRef` gesetzt und weicht die Partition des Aufrufers von der Master-Partition des ComM ab, vermittelt die `SchM` (BSW-Scheduler) den Aufruf inter-core über Cross-Core-Interrupts, Satelliten oder RPC.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise

- **Symbolic Name Generation:** Da `symbolicNameValue = true` gesetzt ist, generiert der BSW-Konfigurator Makros nach dem Schema `ComMConf_ComMUser_<ContainerName>`. Entwickler müssen zwingend diese Makros für Aufrufe von `ComM_RequestComMode()`, `ComM_GetMaxComMode()` und `ComM_GetCurrentComMode()` nutzen.

- **Ressourcenbegrenzung:** Der Parameterbereich `0..255` beschränkt die maximale Useranzahl auf 256. Dies erlaubt stack-intern eine speichereffiziente Repräsentation via `uint8` (`ComM_UserHandleType`).

- **Verbindliche Mindestkonfiguration:** Aufgrund von `lowerMultiplicity = 1` für `ComMUser` schlägt die Validierung fehl, wenn keine User-Instanz definiert ist (selbst bei reinen Gateway- oder Diagnose-Steuergeräten ist mindestens ein Standard-User, z. B. für den DCM, vorgeschrieben).

- **M:N-Zuordnungsmatrix:** Die Verknüpfung erfolgt invertiert (der Kanal referenziert den Nutzer via `ComMUserChannel`). Fehlkonfigurationen (z. B. unreferenzierte User) führen zu totem Code bzw. wirkungslosen `ComM_RequestComMode()`-Aufrufen, die zur Laufzeit `E_NOT_OK` oder DET `COMM_E_WRONG_PARAMETERS` werfen können.

caption: Figure 4: Example for a PNC gateway with not coordinated ComMChannels (see Node2)

lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext
* **Diagrammtyp:** Topologiediagramm / Netzwerk-Architekturschaubild mit Zuordnung von AUTOSAR-ComM-Kanalkonfigurationen (`ComMChannel`) zu partiellen Netzwerkclustern (`ComMPnc`).

* **Technischer Zweck:** Veranschaulichung eines Randfalls im partiellen Netzwerk-Routing (PNC-Gateway nach AUTOSAR Classic ComM). Das Schaubild visualisiert die Konsequenzen, wenn ein Multi-Channel-Knoten (Node2) denselben PNCs (`[PNC1, PNC2]`) auf mehreren Kanälen zugeordnet ist, jedoch **keine** PNC-Gateway-Koordination (`ComMPncGatewayType` nicht konfiguriert) zwischen diesen Kanälen durchführt.

* **Funktionale Einordnung:** AUTOSAR Communication Manager (ComM), Submodul Partial Network Management (Pnm). Es definiert die Schnittstelle zwischen PNC-Zustandsmaschinen, External Request Array (ERA), Internal Request Array (IRA) und den physikalischen `ComMChannel`-Instanzen.
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
* **Knoten / ECUs:**
* **PNC-Coor1 (PNC-Koordinator 1):** Hostet `[PNC1, PNC2]`; Kanäle `Ch1` und `Ch2` jeweils als `ACTIVE` Gateway (`ComMPncGatewayType = COMM_GATEWAY_TYPE_ACTIVE`) konfiguriert.
* **PNC-Coor2 (PNC-Koordinator 2):** Hostet `[PNC1, PNC2]`; besitzt drei Kanäle:
* `Ch1`: Als `PASSIVE` Gateway konfiguriert (`COMM_GATEWAY_TYPE_PASSIVE`), gekoppelt an `PNC-Coor1.Ch1`.
* `Ch2`: Als `ACTIVE` Gateway konfiguriert (`COMM_GATEWAY_TYPE_ACTIVE`), bindet `Node1` an.
* `Ch3`: Als `ACTIVE` Gateway konfiguriert (`COMM_GATEWAY_TYPE_ACTIVE`), bindet den gemeinsamen Bus (Node2, Node3, Node4) an.
* **Node1, Node3, Node4 (Standard-PNC-Knoten):** Single-Channel-Knoten mit `[PNC1, PNC2]`; `ComMPncGatewayType` ist nicht gesetzt (`NONE`).

* **Node2 (Fokus-Knoten, rot hervorgehoben):** Dual-Channel-Knoten (`Ch1`, `Ch2`), beiden Kanälen sind `PNC1` und `PNC2` zugewiesen; an beiden Kanälen ist `ComMPncGatewayType` **nicht gesetzt** (`N`).
* **Konfigurationsparameter & Stereotypen:**
* `ComMPncGatewayType` (Parameter in `ComMChannelPerPnc` bzw. `ComMChannel`):
* `ACTIVE` (Gelb / A): Koordinator leitet interne/externe PNC-Anforderungen aktiv über Netzwerkmanagement-PDUs (NM-PDU / ERA) weiter und hält den Kanal aktiv.
* `PASSIVE` (Blau / P): Empfängt PNC-Anforderungen, spiegelt diese jedoch nicht aktiv zurück bzw. dient als abhängiger Zweig im Koordinationsbaum.
* `NOT set` / `NONE` (Orange / N): Keine Routing- und Aggregationslogik für PNCs zwischen den Kanälen dieses Knotens aktiv.
* **Beziehungen:**
* `PNC-Coor1.Ch2` ist Punkt-zu-Punkt mit `Node2.Ch1` verbunden.
* `PNC-Coor2.Ch3`, `Node2.Ch2`, `Node3.Ch1` und `Node4.Ch1` teilen sich ein physikalisches Multidrop-Bussystem.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
* **Fehlende kanalübergreifende PNC-Zustandssynchronisation in Node2:**

1. **Autarke Kanalzustandsmaschinen:** Da Node2 kein Gateway ist, wertet `ComM` in Node2 Anfragen (ERA/IRA) pro Kanal isoliert aus. Es findet kein interner Transfer von PNC-Zuständen zwischen `Ch1` und `Ch2` statt.
2. **Anforderungs-Pfad A (über PNC-Coor1):** Wird ein PNC auf `PNC-Coor1` aktiv, sendet dieser NM-Vektoren über `Ch2` an `Node2.Ch1`. `Node2.Ch1` wechselt in `COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION`.

3. **Problemfall Asynchronität:** Solange `PNC-Coor2` (oder ein anderer Busteilnehmer) denselben PNC nicht gleichzeitig auf dem unteren Bus anfordert, verbleibt `Node2.Ch2` in `COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION` bzw. `COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION`.

4. **Applikations-Erwartungsbruch:** Eine SW-C auf Node2, die `ComM_RequestComMode(..., COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION)` für `PNC1` ausführt oder sich auf die Verfügbarkeit von `PNC1` verlässt, erwartet deterministisch, dass **alle** diesem PNC zugeordneten Kommunikationskanäle betriebsbereit sind. Ohne Gateway-Kopplung in Node2 ist dies verletzt, falls die Koordinatoren die Kanäle nicht strikt zeitsynchron ansteuern.
* **Terminierungs- / Release-Phase:**
* Wird der PNC auf `Ch1` freigegeben, schaltet `Node2.Ch1` nach Ablauf des `ComMPncPrepareSleepTimer` ab, während `Node2.Ch2` ggf. noch aktiv bleibt.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise
* **System- & Kommunikationsdesign (System Description / Fibex / ARXML):**

* Werden einem PNC in einer ECU mehrere `ComMChannels` zugeordnet, ohne dass `ComMPncGatewayType` gesetzt ist, **muss** die Gesamtsystemarchitektur (Cluster-Topologie und Scheduling der NM-Botschaften über alle Koordinatoren) garantieren, dass diese Kanäle immer exakt zum selben Zeitpunkt angefordert und freigegeben werden.
* **Stack-Konfiguration (`ComM`):**
* Fehlt diese globale Koordination, darf `Node2` nicht als unkoordinierter Dual-Channel-Knoten für denselben PNC konfiguriert werden. Die Lösung erfordert entweder:
* Setzen von `ComMPncGatewayType` auf `ACTIVE` an mindestens einem der Ports von Node2 (sofern Node2 als Gateway agieren soll/darf), oder
* Auftrennung der PNC-IDs, sodass `PNC1`/`PNC2` nicht mehrdeutig über unkoordinierte Kanäle derselben ECU aufgespannt werden.
* **Applikations-Vertrag (SW-C zu ComM):**

* Applikationen fordern PNCs an, keine `ComMChannels`. ComM übernimmt bei fehlender Gateway-Konfiguration explizit keine Verantwortung für die Harmonisierung unkoordinierter Kanäle. Embedded-Entwickler dürfen in SW-Cs keine manuelle Kanalüberwachung implementieren, sondern müssen den Designfehler im ARXML-Extrakt adressieren.

    * `NOT set` / `NONE` (Orange / N): Keine Routing- und Aggregationslogik für PNCs zwischen den Kanälen dieses Knotens aktiv.
* **Beziehungen:**
  * `PNC-Coor1.Ch2` ist Punkt-zu-Punkt mit `Node2.Ch1` verbunden.
  * `PNC-Coor2.Ch3`, `Node2.Ch2`, `Node3.Ch1` und `Node4.Ch1` teilen sich ein physikalisches Multidrop-Bussystem.

---

### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf

* **Fehlende kanalübergreifende PNC-Zustandssynchronisation in Node2:**
  1. **Autarke Kanalzustandsmaschinen:** Da Node2 kein Gateway ist, wertet `ComM` in Node2 Anfragen (ERA/IRA) pro Kanal isoliert aus. Es findet kein interner Transfer von PNC-Zuständen zwischen `Ch1` und `Ch2` statt.
  2. **Anforderungs-Pfad A (über PNC-Coor1):** Wird ein PNC auf `PNC-Coor1` aktiv, sendet dieser NM-Vektoren über `Ch2` an `Node2.Ch1`. `Node2.Ch1` wechselt in `COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION`.
  3. **Problemfall Asynchronität:** Solange `PNC-Coor2` (oder ein anderer Busteilnehmer) denselben PNC nicht gleichzeitig auf dem unteren Bus anfordert, verbleibt `Node2.Ch2` in `COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION` bzw. `COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION`.
  4. **Applikations-Erwartungsbruch:** Eine SW-C auf Node2, die `ComM_RequestComMode(..., COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION)` für `PNC1` ausführt oder sich auf die Verfügbarkeit von `PNC1` verlässt, erwartet deterministisch, dass **alle** diesem PNC zugeordneten Kommunikationskanäle betriebsbereit sind. Ohne Gateway-Kopplung in Node2 ist dies verletzt, falls die Koordinatoren die Kanäle nicht strikt zeitsynchron ansteuern.
* **Terminierungs- / Release-Phase:**
  * Wird der PNC auf `Ch1` freigegeben, schaltet `Node2.Ch1` nach Ablauf des `ComMPncPrepareSleepTimer` ab, während `Node2.Ch2` ggf. noch aktiv bleibt.

---

### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise

* **System- & Kommunikationsdesign (System Description / Fibex / ARXML):**
  * Werden einem PNC in einer ECU mehrere `ComMChannels` zugeordnet, ohne dass `ComMPncGatewayType` gesetzt ist, **muss** die Gesamtsystemarchitektur (Cluster-Topologie und Scheduling der NM-Botschaften über alle Koordinatoren) garantieren, dass diese Kanäle immer exakt zum selben Zeitpunkt angefordert und freigegeben werden.
* **Stack-Konfiguration (`ComM`):**
  * Fehlt diese globale Koordination, darf `Node2` nicht als unkoordinierter Dual-Channel-Knoten für denselben PNC konfiguriert werden. Die Lösung erfordert entweder:
    * Setzen von `ComMPncGatewayType` auf `ACTIVE` an mindestens einem der Ports von Node2 (sofern Node2 als Gateway agieren soll/darf), oder
    * Auftrennung der PNC-IDs, sodass `PNC1`/`PNC2` nicht mehrdeutig über unkoordinierte Kanäle derselben ECU aufgespannt werden.
* **Applikations-Vertrag (SW-C zu ComM):**
  * Applikationen fordern PNCs an, keine `ComMChannels`. ComM übernimmt bei fehlender Gateway-Konfiguration explizit keine Verantwortung für die Harmonisierung unkoordinierter Kanäle. Embedded-Entwickler dürfen in SW-Cs keine manuelle Kanalüberwachung implementieren, sondern müssen den Designfehler im ARXML-Extrakt adressieren.

lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext

UML-Sequenzdiagramm (Interaktionsdiagramm) im Kontext der AUTOSAR Classic Platform Communication Stack (BSW) Architektur. Das Diagramm spezifiziert das synchrone und asynchrone Weiterleiten (Gatewaying) einer I-PDU von einem CAN-Netzwerk (CAN1) auf ein zweites CAN-Netzwerk (CAN2) bei simultanem lokalem Empfang durch das obere Kommunikationsmodul COM (1:N-Multicast-Routing / Fan-Out im PduR).
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
Beteiligte Komponenten (Module/Lifelines):
- `«module» Com`: AUTOSAR Communication Module als oberer Kommunikations-Layer (Upper Layer).
- `«module» PduR`: PDU Router als zentrale Routing-Instanz im BSW-Kommunikationsstack.
- `«module» CanIf`: CAN Interface als unterer Layer (Lower Layer) für die beiden Netzwerkanbindungen CAN1 und CAN2.
Schnittstellen & Interaktionen:
- `PduR_<User:Lo>RxIndication(PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)`: Callback des CanIf an den PduR bei PDU-Empfang auf CAN1.
- `Com_RxIndication(PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)`: Synchrone Weiterleitung der I-PDU vom PduR an Com.

- `CanIf_Transmit(Std_ReturnType, PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)`: Sendeaufruf des PduR an CanIf für CAN2 (im UML-Diagramm ist der C-Rückgabewert `Std_ReturnType` als erster Methodenparameter modelliert).
- `copy data()`: Interne synchrone Operation des CanIf zur Pufferung/Kopie der Nutzdaten in den CAN2-Sendepuffer.
- `PduR_<User:Lo>TxConfirmation(PduIdType)`: Asynchroner Bestätigungs-Callback des CanIf an den PduR nach erfolgreicher Aussendung auf CAN2.
Diagramm-Annotationen:
- "Received on CAN1"
- "The PDU Router module routes to COM first because of the lower routing path ID"
- "Transmisison request on CAN2"
- "Transmission is confirmed on CAN2"
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
1. CanIf empfängt eine I-PDU auf CAN1 und ruft synchron `PduR_<User:Lo>RxIndication(PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)` auf.

2. Der PduR löst das 1:N-Routing deterministisch anhand der konfigurierten `PduRRoutingPathId` auf. Da der Pfad zum COM-Modul die niedrigere Routing-Path-ID aufweist, wird zuerst synchron `Com_RxIndication(PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)` aufgerufen.
3. Com verarbeitet die I-PDU synchron und gibt den Kontrollfluss an den PduR zurück.
4. Anschließend bedient der PduR den Pfad mit der höheren ID und initiiert die Weitersendung auf CAN2 über `CanIf_Transmit(Std_ReturnType, PduIdType, const PduInfoType*)`.
5. CanIf puffert die PDU-Daten synchron via `copy data()` und kehrt mit `Std_ReturnType` zum PduR zurück.
6. Der PduR schließt seine Empfangsroutine ab und kehrt synchron zu CanIf (CAN1-Kontext) zurück.
7. Nach physikalischer Aussendung auf CAN2 bestätigt CanIf die Übertragung asynchron mittels `PduR_<User:Lo>TxConfirmation(PduIdType)` an den PduR, der die Bestätigung abwickelt und zurückkehrt.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise

- Routing-Reihenfolge: Bei 1:N-Fan-Out schreibt AUTOSAR normativ vor, dass Routing-Pfade strikt aufsteigend nach ihrer konfigurierten `PduRRoutingPathId` abgearbeitet werden. Falls Verarbeitungsabhängigkeiten (z. B. lokale Signalverarbeitung vor Weiterleitung) bestehen, müssen Integratoren dies zwingend über die ID-Reihenfolge in der ARXML-Konfiguration sicherstellen.

- Ausführungskontext: Sämtliche Aufrufe (`Com_RxIndication`, `CanIf_Transmit`) liegen synchron im Empfangskontext des CAN1-Treibers (ISR oder MainFunction). Keines der Module darf blockierende Operationen ausführen.

- Pufferkonsistenz: CanIf muss die Nutzdaten bei `CanIf_Transmit` unverzüglich per `copy data()` lokal kopieren, da der PduInfoType-Zeiger nach Rückkehr aus `PduR_<User:Lo>RxIndication` seine Gültigkeit verliert.

- API-Modellierung: Der erste Parameter `Std_ReturnType` in `CanIf_Transmit` repräsentiert den Funktionsrückgabewert der AUTOSAR-C-Schnittstelle `Std_ReturnType CanIf_Transmit(PduIdType TxPduId, const PduInfoType* PduInfoPtr)`.

lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext
* **Klassifikation:** AUTOSAR ECUC Metamodell-Ausschnitt (UML-Klassendiagramm für BswM/ECUC Parameter Definition, Stereotypen `EcucParamConfContainerDef` und `EcucReferenceDef`).
* **Technischer Zweck:** Spezifikation der Konfigurationsstruktur des Communication Managers (`ComM`) im System Services Layer (AUTOSAR Classic Platform, Release R21-11).

* **Funktionale Einordnung:** Definiert die statische Zuordnung zwischen Kommunikationsbenutzern (`ComMUser`), physikalischen Kommunikationskanälen (`ComMChannel`) und Teilnetzwerk-Clustern (`ComMPnc`). Es modelliert sowohl das direkte Kanal-Mapping als auch das indirekte Mapping über Partial Network Cluster (PNC).
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
#### Container-Definitionen (`EcucParamConfContainerDef`)
* Repräsentiert Software-Komponenten (SWCs) oder BSW-Module (z. B. DCM), die Kommunikationsmodi anfordern (`ComM_UserHandleType`).
* *Hinweis Metamodell:* Die Obergrenze 65635 ist eine formale Spezifikationsgrenze (uint16-Wertebereich + formaler Offset).
* **`ComMChannel` [1..256]:**
* Physikalische Kommunikationsschnittstelle (CAN, LIN, FlexRay, Ethernet) zu den jeweiligen Bus State Managern (`CanSM`, `LinSM`, `FrSM`, `EthSM`).
* Mindestens ein Kanal ist obligatorisch (`lowerMultiplicity = 1`).
* **`ComMUserPerChannel` [0..255]:**
* Sub-Container unterhalb von `ComMChannel` (`+subContainer`), der die Kanal-zu-Benutzer-Zuordnungen kapselt.
* Definiert ein Partial Network Cluster (PNC). Die Obergrenze 504 korrespondiert mit der maximalen Bitanzahl des PNC-Vektors (63 Bytes × 8 Bits = 504 PNCs gemäß AUTOSAR COM/PDU-Router-Spezifikation).
#### Referenz-Definitionen (`EcucReferenceDef`)
* **`ComMUserChannel` [1..1] (innerhalb `ComMUserPerChannel`):**
* `+reference` in `ComMUserPerChannel`, navigiert über `+destination` auf `ComMUser`.
* Realisiert die direkte $n:m$-Zuordnung eines Benutzers zu einem Kanal.
* **`ComMChannelPerPnc` [0..255]:**
* `+reference` in `ComMPnc`, navigiert über `+destination` auf `ComMChannel`.
* Weist dem PNC die physikalischen Buskanäle zu, auf denen das Teilnetzwerk aktiv ist.
* **`ComMUserPerPnc` [0..255] (`ECUC_ComM_00874`):**
* `+reference` in `ComMPnc`, navigiert über `+destination` auf `ComMUser`.
* Verknüpft Benutzer direkt mit dem logischen Teilnetzwerk.
#### Beziehungssemantik
* **Kompositionen (ausgefüllte Rauten):** Baumartige Schachtelung im ARXML-Dokument (`EcucParamConfContainerDef` aggregiert Kind-Container oder Parameter-/Referenzdefinitionen).
* **Assoziationen (`+destination` Pfeile):** Typisierte Referenzen (`EcucReferenceDef`) auf die Ziel-Container-Instanzen.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
Aus dem statischen Metamodell leitet der BSW-Generator Zuordnungstabellen für die Laufzeit ab:
1. **Modusanforderung (Direkter Pfad):**
* Aufruf: `ComM_RequestComMode(ComMUser, COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION)`.
* Lookup über `ComMUserPerChannel` / `ComMUserChannel`.
* Evaluation der Kanalzustände: Falls Kanal in `COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION`, erfolgt Triggerung des Bus-Zustandsautomaten via `<Bus>SM_RequestComMode(NetworkHandle, COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION)`.
2. **Modusanforderung (PNC-Pfad bei `ComMPncEnabled == TRUE`):**
* Aufruf: `ComM_RequestComMode(ComMUser, COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION)`.
* Lookup über `ComMUserPerPnc`: Ermittlung aller referenzierten `ComMPnc`-Instanzen.
* Pro betroffenem PNC werden über `ComMChannelPerPnc` die zugehörigen physikalischen Kanäle ermittelt und aggregiert angefordert.
* Triggerung der PNC-Zustandsmaschine (PNC Full Communication) und Freigabe der Signalübertragung (EIRA/ERA) über die Com-Schnittstelle.
3. **Abschaltpfad (`COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION`):**

* Modusfreigabe erfolgt erst, wenn alle referenzierten `ComMUser` eines Kanals bzw. eines PNCs den Modus `COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION` angefordert haben und Nachlaufzeiten (`ComMNmLightTimeout`, MinFullCom-Timer) abgelaufen sind.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise
* **Kanal- und User-Limits im BSW-Stack:**
* Kanäle sind auf max. 256 beschränkt $\rightarrow$ Repräsentiert als `NetworkHandleType` (typischerweise `uint8`, Werte 0..255).
* PNCs sind auf max. 504 beschränkt $\rightarrow$ Erfordert für `PNCHandleType` zwingend `uint16`.
* **Generator-Optimierung & Speicherbedarf:**
* Der Code-Generator (BSW-Gen) erzeugt aus diesen Abhängigkeiten Bitmasken oder flache Indextabellen (`ComM_UserChannelMapping[]`, `ComM_PncChannelMapping[]`).

* Unnötig definierte Querverweise (`ComMUserPerChannel` parallel zu redundanten `ComMUserPerPnc`) vergrößern die ROM-Tabellen und verlängern die Iterationszeit in den zyklischen Main-Functions (`ComM_MainFunction_<Channel>`).
* **SWS-Anforderungen:**
* `ECUC_ComM_00843`: Erzwingt, dass `ComMUserChannel` ein gültiges Ziel vom Typ `ComMUser` referenzieren muss.
* `ECUC_ComM_00874`: Regelt die Zuweisung von `ComMUser` zu `ComMPnc`.
* **Konfigurationsregel:**

* Ist PNC aktiviert, sollte die Zuordnung prioritär über `ComMPnc` erfolgen. Direkte Kanalzuordnungen (`ComMUserPerChannel`) für denselben Nutzer führen dazu, dass Kanäle dauerhaft im Vollkommunikationsmodus gehalten werden, selbst wenn das Teilnetzwerk schlafen könnte.

Das Modul COM ist im Communication Service Layer zwischen der RTE (oben) und dem PDU-Router `PduR` (unten) angesiedelt; es abstrahiert I-PDUs in Signale/Signalgruppen und steuert Signal-Gatewaying sowie PDU-Gruppen.
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
Das Diagramm definiert die Metamodell-Elemente zur Konfiguration des COM-Stacks:
- **Wurzelmodul:**
- `Com` (`EcucModuleDef`, Multiplizität: `0..1`): Repräsentiert die gesamte COM-Moduldefinition eines ECUs.
- **Top-Level-Container (Komposition via `+container`):**

- `ComGeneral` (`EcucParamConfContainerDef`, Multiplizität: `1..1`): Invariante, modulweite Compile-Time-Parameter (z. B. APIs für Versionsabfrage, Minimal-Delay-Timer-Verhalten, Dev-Error-Detect-Aktivierung).
- `ComConfig` (`EcucParamConfContainerDef`, Multiplizität: `1..1`): Wurzelcontainer für die funktionale Kommunikationsmatrix (Post-Build- bzw. Link-Time-Konfiguration).
- **Sub-Container von `ComConfig` (Komposition via `+subContainer`, Multiplizität jeweils `0..*`):**
- `ComSignal`: Definition einzelner Applikationssignale (Bitposition, Länge, Byte-Order, Update-Bits, Filter, Timeouts, Transfer-Properties wie `PENDING`/`TRIGGERED`).
- `ComSignalGroup`: Atomare Zusammenfassung mehrerer Signale zur konsistenten Übertragung via Shadow-Buffer-APIs (`Com_UpdateShadowSignal`, `Com_SendSignalGroup`).
- `ComIPdu`: Definition von Interaktions-Layer-PDUs (Richtung `SEND`/`RECEIVE`, PDU-Länge, Callbacks zu PduR, Übertragungsmodi: `PERIODIC`, `DIRECT`, `MIXED`, `NONE`).
- `ComIPduGroup`: Logische Bündelung von IPDUs zur Laufzeit-Steuerung über BswM/RTE (`Com_IpduGroupStart`/`Com_IpduGroupStop`).
- `ComGwMapping`: Routing-Konfiguration für Signal-to-Signal- und Signalgruppen-Gatewaying direkt im COM-Modul (ohne RTE-Beteiligung).
- `ComMainFunctionRx`: Konfigurationsinstanzen für zyklische Empfangsverarbeitung (Deadline Monitoring, RX-Signal-Entpacken).
- `ComMainFunctionTx`: Konfigurationsinstanzen für zyklische Sendeabläufe (Periodische Triggerung, Minimal-Delay-Timer, TX-Timeouts).
- `ComMainFunctionRouteSignals`: Konfigurationsinstanzen für das Entkoppeln und periodische Ausführen von Signal-Gateway-Routings.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
Obgleich es sich um ein statisches Konfigurationsmodell handelt, determiniert die Entitäten-Struktur die Laufzeitarchitektur:

- **Multi-Rate & Multi-Core Entkopplung:** Durch Multiplizität `0..*` bei `ComMainFunctionRx`, `ComMainFunctionTx` und `ComMainFunctionRouteSignals` können dedizierte periodische BSW-Schedulables generiert werden (`Com_MainFunctionRx_<id>()`, `Com_MainFunctionTx_<id>()`, `Com_MainFunctionRouteSignals_<id>()`). Dies ermöglicht die Zuweisung zu unterschiedlichen OS-Tasks, Zykluszeiten und Prozessor-Cores.
- **RX-Pfad:**
1. Asynchron: `PduR_ComRxIndication()` puffert I-PDU.
2. Synchron/Zyklisch: Aufruf von `ComMainFunctionRx` validiert Update-Bits, führt Deadline-Monitoring aus, entpackt `ComSignal`/`ComSignalGroup` und meldet Signal-Timeouts via Dem/Det bzw. Callback.
- **TX-Pfad:**
1. RTE schreibt via `Com_SendSignal()` / `Com_SendSignalGroup()`.
2. Abhängig von `ComSignal.ComTransferProperty` sofortiger PDU-Trigger oder Verzögerung auf den nächsten Zyklus der zugeordneten `ComMainFunctionTx`.
3. `ComMainFunctionTx` prüft Minimal-Delay-Timer (MDT) und ruft `PduR_ComTransmit()`.
- **Gateway-Pfad:**
1. `ComGwMapping` verknüpft Quell- und Zielsignale.
2. Die periodische Ausführung von `ComMainFunctionRouteSignals` transferiert und konvertiert Daten gepuffert zwischen RX- und TX-IPDUs.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise

- **Generator- & Toolchain-Vertrag:** Das Diagramm erzwingt, dass alle Signal-, PDU- und Routing-Definitionen hierarchisch unter `ComConfig` aggregiert werden müssen. Ein AUTOSAR-Konfigurator darf Signale nicht direkt unter `Com` einhängen.

- **Speicherorganisation & Variantenmanagement:** `ComGeneral` ist `VARIANT-PRE-COMPILE`. `ComConfig` erlaubt je nach Implementierung `VARIANT-POST-BUILD` (z. B. austauschbare Routingtabellen oder PDU-Layouts im Flash ohne Rekompilierung des Basiscodes).

- **Task-Design im OS:** Entwickler müssen für jede instanziierte `ComMainFunctionRx/Tx/RouteSignals` einen korrespondierenden OS-Task und ein BSW-Schedule-Event im RTE/BswM-Modul konfigurieren. Fehlende MainFunctions bei vorhandenen PDUs führen zu blockierten Timeouts und ausbleibendem periodischen Versand.

- **Gateway-Performanz:** Durch getrennte `ComMainFunctionRouteSignals`-Instanzen kann signalbasiertes Routing isoliert von Standard-TX/RX-Tasks mit angepassten Zykluszeiten betrieben werden, um Latenzen zu minimieren und Core-Lasten zu balancieren.

lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext
* **Diagrammtyp:** UML-Klassendiagramm / AUTOSAR ECUC Parameter Definition Metamodell (Auszug aus der BSW-Moduldefinition `EcucModuleDef`).

* **Technischer Zweck:** Definition der statischen Konfigurationsstruktur des Moduls `Com` für den Container `ComGeneral`. Es spezifiziert Typen, Wertebereiche, Multiplizitäten und Default-Werte jener Parameter, die das globale funktionale Verhalten, den generierten API-Umfang sowie den Pre-Compile-Footprint des AUTOSAR COM-Stacks (Communication Layer) steuern.

* **Architektur-Einordnung:** Schnittstelle zwischen AUTOSAR-Metamodellwerkzeugen (Generatoren) und dem BSW-Modul COM. COM vermittelt signalspezifische Zugriffe (RTE/SWC-Ebene) an I-PDUs der unteren Schicht (PDU-Router / `PduR`).
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
#### Metamodell-Klassen & Container
* **`Com: EcucModuleDef`** (Multiplizität: `0..1`): Wurzelknoten der COM-Modulkonfigurationsdefinition.
* **`ComGeneral: EcucParamConfContainerDef`** (Multiplizität: `1..1`): Mandatorischer globaler Singleton-Konfigurationscontainer für generelle Stack-Eigenschaften.
* **Beziehung:** Strenge Komposition (`+container`, Kardinalität `1..1`) von `Com` zu `ComGeneral`.
#### Konfigurationsparameter (`+parameter`, Aggregationen von `ComGeneral`)
1. **`ComCancellationSupport: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..1`, `defaultValue = true`.
* Aktiviert das Zurückziehen anstehender Sendeanforderungen (`PduR_ComCancelTransmit`).
2. **`ComConfigurationUseDet: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..1`.
* Schaltet die Meldung von Entwicklungsfehlern an den Default Error Tracer (`Det_ReportError`) scharf.
3. **`ComEnableMDTForCyclicTransmission: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..1`, `defaultValue = true`.
* Erzwingt die Einhaltung der Minimum Delay Time (MDT) auch für rein periodische Sende-PDUs (`PERIODIC` / `MIXED`).
4. **`ComRetryFailedTransmitRequests: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..1`, `defaultValue = false`.
* Steuert, ob bei negativem Rückgabewert von `PduR_ComTransmit` ein erneuter Sendeversuch im nachfolgenden `Com_MainFunctionTx`-Zyklus erfolgt.
5. **`ComSupportedIPduGroups: EcucIntegerParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `1..1`, Wertebereich: `0 .. 65535`.
* Maximale Dimensionierung der verwaltbaren I-PDU-Gruppen (Bitfeldbreite für Start-/Stopp-Vektoren).
6. **`ComUserCbkHeaderFile: EcucStringParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..*`, Längenbeschränkung: `1 .. 32` Zeichen.
* Spezifiziert einzubindende C-Header-Dateien für anwendungsspezifische Callbacks (z. B. Timeout- und Notification-Routinen).
7. **`ComEnableSignalGroupArrayApi: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `1..1`, `defaultValue = false`.
* Generiert Array-basierte Zugriffsfunktionen (`Com_SendSignalGroupArray`, `Com_ReceiveSignalGroupArray`) zur Optimierung von Serialisierungsoverhead (Zero-Copy-Arrayzugriff).
8. **`ComVersionInfoApi: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `1..1`, `defaultValue = false`.
* Aktiviert den Service `Com_GetVersionInfo()`.
9. **`ComMetaDataSupport: EcucBooleanParamDef`**
* Multiplizität: `0..1`, `defaultValue = false`.
* Aktiviert die Verarbeitung dynamischer PDU-Metadaten (z. B. CAN-ID, Quell-/Zieladressen in J1939/DoIP) zwischen RTE und PduR.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
Als statisches Konfigurationsmetamodell besitzt das Diagramm keine direkte Laufzeit-Zustandsdynamik. Die Parameter determinieren jedoch folgende Ablaufpfade und Trigger:

* **Fehlerpfad (`ComConfigurationUseDet == true`):** Laufzeitprüfungen in allen `Com_*`-APIs rufen bei Parametrierfehlern synchron `Det_ReportError` auf; bei `false` werden diese Checks zwecks Codegrößen- und Laufzeitoptimierung auskompiliert.
* **Transmissionsfluss (`ComRetryFailedTransmitRequests`):**
1. Triggerung von `PduR_ComTransmit` im Rahmen von `Com_SendSignal` oder `Com_MainFunctionTx`.
2. Gibt `PduR_ComTransmit` den Status `E_NOT_OK` zurück:
* Wenn `true`: PDU-Status wird als *pending retry* markiert; Re-Transmission erfolgt im nächsten Task-Zyklus von `Com_MainFunctionTx`.
* Wenn `false`: Verwerfen der Sendeanforderung ohne Neuversuch.
* **MDT-Überwachung (`ComEnableMDTForCyclicTransmission`):**
* Verhindert bei `true` Bus-Überlastungen, wenn zyklische Sende-Timer ablaufen, während der MDT-Timer noch aktiv ist (zyklischer Sendeanstoß wird verzögert, bis MDT abgelaufen ist).
* **Cancellation-Pfad (`ComCancellationSupport == true`):**
* Ermöglicht das synchrone/asynchrone Abbrechen niederpriorer Übertragungen via `PduR_ComCancelTransmit`.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise
* **Pre-Compile-Schalter (Code- und RAM-Footprint):**

* `ComVersionInfoApi`, `ComConfigurationUseDet` und `ComEnableSignalGroupArrayApi` fungieren als direkte Präprozessor-Makros (z. B. `COM_VERSION_INFO_API == STD_ON`). Bei Deaktivierung entfallen die zugehörigen API-Einsprungpunkte und ROM-Tabellen vollständig.
* **Signal Group Performance:**

* Bei strukturierten Datenpaketen / komplexen Signalgruppen zwingend `ComEnableSignalGroupArrayApi = true` setzen. Andernfalls müssen Signalgruppen per Shadow-Buffer elementweise kopiert werden (`Com_UpdateShadowSignal`), was signifikanten Laufzeit-Overhead im RTE-Task erzeugt.
* **PDU-Gruppen-Dimensionierung (`ComSupportedIPduGroups`):**

* Definiert direkt die Größe des internen I-PDU-Gruppenvektors (`uint8[]` bzw. `uint32[]`) zur Laufzeit. Zu hoch gewählte Werte vergrößern den RAM-Footprint des Stacks unnötig; zu niedrig gewählte Werte führen zu Validierungsfehlern im Generator bei Überschreiten der Gruppenanzahl.
* **Include-Hierarchie (`ComUserCbkHeaderFile`):**

* Jeder konfigurierte Header muss im Compiler-Suchpfad liegen und exakt die Funktionsprototypen deklarieren, die in den COM-Signal-/PDU-Konfigurationen als Callbacks (`ComNotification`, `ComTimeoutNotification` etc.) referenziert werden, um implizite Deklarationswarnungen (MISRA C:2012 Rule 8.4) zu verhindern.

lines: ### 1. Diagrammtyp & Architektur-Kontext

Schichten- und Interaktionsdiagramm für die AUTOSAR Classic Platform. Das Diagramm illustriert das Routing und die Zuordnung von I-PDU-IDs im Kommunikationsstapel zwischen COM, PDU Router (PduR) und CAN Interface (CanIf).
### 2. Komponenten, Entitäten & Schnittstellen
- **COM**: Oberes Kommunikationsmodul (Upper Layer BSW).
- **PduR**: Zentraler PDU-Router zur Weiterleitung und ID-Umsetzung.
- **CanIf**: Unteres Schnittstellenmodul für den CAN-Bus (Lower Layer BSW).
- **Schnittstellen**:
- `PduR Transmit(11)`: Aufruf von COM an PduR mit der I-PDU-ID 11.
- `CanIf Transmit(22)`: Aufruf von PduR an CanIf mit der umgesetzten I-PDU-ID 22.
- `PduR CanIfTxConfirmation(42)`: Bestätigungsaufruf von CanIf an PduR mit der I-PDU-ID 42.
- `Com TxConfirmation(32)`: Bestätigungsaufruf von PduR an COM mit der I-PDU-ID 32.
### 3. Dynamisches Verhalten & Sequenzablauf
1. COM initiiert das Senden einer I-PDU durch Aufruf von `PduR Transmit(11)`.
2. PduR übersetzt die konfigurierte I-PDU-ID (11) für die Ziel-Schnittstelle und ruft `CanIf Transmit(22)` auf.
3. Nach erfolgreicher Übertragung meldet CanIf den Vollzug über `PduR CanIfTxConfirmation(42)` an PduR zurück.
4. PduR leitet die Sendebestätigung an das Ursprungsmodul weiter und ruft `Com TxConfirmation(32)` auf.
### 4. Normative Relevanz & Entwickler-Hinweise

Das Diagramm veranschaulicht beispielhaft, dass I-PDU-IDs modul- und schnittstellenspezifisch konfiguriert sind. Jedes beteiligte BSW-Modul (COM, PduR, CanIf) nutzt für dieselbe logische PDU im Sende- und Bestätigungspfad eigene numerische Bezeichner, die bei der Konfiguration in der Routingtabelle des PduR aufeinander abgebildet werden müssen. Die Funktionsnamen sind im Diagramm mit Leerzeichen statt Unterstrichen dargestellt.

Figure 8.2: Example of a the communication of a mode from the "ECU State Manager" Service-component to an application software-component For mode switch interfaces, only 1:n communication (1 mode manager and n mode users, with n≥ 0) is possible. The single mode manager owns the current mode of the ModeDeclarationGroup. The users are informed of any mode switch of the manager. For the mode managers of the AUTOSAR basic software, there is typically for each mode switch based service also a sender receiver based service to request a mode. E.g., for each ComM user one mode switch interface indicates the currently available communication mode and a sender receiver interface is used to request the desired communication mode. In this pattern there is usually one mode requestor that is at the same time a mode user. Figure 8.3 shows this pattern for the ComM.

Figure 8.3: Example of a the communication of a mode from the “ECU State Manager” Service-component to an application software-component Due to the strong synchronization between a mode manager and the mode users, mode switch communication is only supported in ECU local communication. For a mode management that spans several ECUs, a communication pattern including service software proxy components for the distribution of mode requests and the BswM for the switching of modes on each ECU is recommended (see section 7.2.3).

3.4.2.3 Synchronized PNC shutdown
In order to avoid timeout failure on application level, the PNC shall shutdown in a synchronized way (all nodes in the PNC will shutdown at the same point in time). The synchronized PNC shutdown is a functionality which is a cooperation of ComM, Nm and <Bus>Nm to ensure a synchronized PNC shutdown at almost the same point in time across the whole PN topology. A synchronized PNC shutdown is handled by ECUs in role of a top-level PNC coordinator or intermediate PNC coordinator if the PNC Gateway is enabled. If the ComM of an ECU in the role of a top-level PNC coordinator detects that a PNC is released (PNC is no longer internally or externally requested), the ComM requests a synchronized PNC shutdown. The Nm module stores all requests and handles them in the context of the Nm_Mainfunction. The Nm module indicates the affected <Bus>Nms regarding an activated PNC shutdown process. The <Bus>Nms call the Nm module to provide the aggregated requests for a synchronized PNC shutdown as PNC bit vector per given NM-Channel. The <Bus>Nms use the provided PNC bit vector to assemble a NM-PDU as PN shutdown message and transmit this message on the according NM channel. If a PN shutdown message is received by an ECU in the role of an intermediate PNC coordinator, the <Bus>Nms extract the PNC bit vector from the received PN shutdown message and forwards the information by calling the callback function Nm_ForwardSynchronizedPncShutdown. The callback function will immediately forward the indication to ComM by calling ComM_Nm_ForwardSynchronizedPncShutdown. ComM will immediately request a synchronized PNC shutdown of all actively PNC coordinated (coordinated by a PNC gateway) ComMChannels. The requests for a synchronized PNC shutdown are forwarded to the Nm module per NM-Channel and handled in the same way as described in the previous section. If a PNC leaf node receives a PN shutdown message, then it will handle the message as a usual NM message (update the local PN info and reset PN reset time).

3.4.3 Scheduling of main functions
Since state changes of communication channels or PNCs are generally processed in the context of the main processing functions, it is important to properly consider the scheduling and the order of execution for the main processing functions for the modules involved in the communication and network management (ComM, Nm, <Bus>Nms). ComM generally coordinates the activities considering the events in the system and triggers the required actions (by calling the relevant APIs) of the lower layers. Events in the system causing specific actions required to be triggered by ComM can be internal requests of users (internal requests for channels or PNCs), passive/external requests for channels or PNCs or synchronized PNC shutdown messages received on the bus. External events may be caused by wakeup events, reception of cyclic NM messages or synchronized shutdown messages. ComM receives and processes all internal and external requests and triggers required actions that will lead to state changes in the state machines for communication and network management modules and consequently the transmission of cyclic NM messages or synchronized shutdown messages on the bus. 5.2.1.2.4 CAN State Manager
Detection Notified by CanSm_ControllerBusOff(controller) (seeCAN Interface above) Reaction
• Count the bus-off events
• Start the error recovery mechanism Report
• If the error is confirmed, it is reported to the DEM. If the recovery succeeds, the event is cleared from the DEM (see [SWS_CanSM_00605], [SWS_CanSM_00498],
[SWS_CanSM_00522]). The DEM event for this error is configured per CAN network in the CANSM_E_BUS_OFF (see
[ECUC_CanSM_00070]).
• CANSM informs the Communication Manager about the communication status (COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION) notified with ComM_BusSM_ModeIndication (see
[SWS_CanSM_00521])
• CANSM informs the BSW State Manager of the BusOff event (with BswM_CanSM_CurrentState) (see [SWS_CanSM_00508]) Recovery
[SWS_CanSM_00509] The CAN State Manager controls the error recovery mechanism, which includes
• a reset of the CAN controller: CanIf_SetControllerMode(..., CANSM_CS_STARTED)
• disabling/enabling the transmit path: CanIf_SetPduMode(...,CANIF_SET_TX_OFFLINE/ CANIF_SET_TX_ONLINE)

5.2.2.2.2 CAN Interface
Detection There is no timeout detection by CanIf Reaction There is no reaction performed by CanIf Report The CanIf does not report any timeout event to the upper layers. Recovery The recovery is triggered by the CAN State Manager:
• CanIf_SetControllerMode(Controller, CANIF_CS_STARTED).
• Can_InitController(Controller, *Config).
• Can_SetControllerMode (Controller, CAN_T_STARTED).

7.1.5 Goto sleep
The goto-sleep sequence differs between master and slave nodes. In a master node, when the ComM module requests the no communication mode, the LinSM will request the goto-sleep command to be sent on the LIN bus. In a slave node, the LIN Interface indicates the bus sleep event to LinSM, either caused by reception of a goto-sleep command or by detection of a bus idle condition. If the ComM module has requested the no communication mode before, the bus sleep event is forwarded to ComM. Otherwise if the full communication mode requested by Com M module is active, the bus sleep event is not forwarded to ComM, but the wakeup process is restarted by LinSM after the goto-sleep sequence is completed. In all cases, the entering of the no communication mode is notified to BswM and Com M. The callback will always be made, even if there was a problem.

7.1 Partial Network Cluster Management
The ComM offers users the option to wake and keep awake so-called "partial network cluster" (PNC). A PNC is a (logical) group of ECUs which have to be active at the same time to realize some distributed functionality. If PNC-enabled gateways are used, a PNC can span the whole network (different busses on different topology levels of the network hierarchy). Without the PN functionality, NM messages can only wake and keep awake whole busses.

7.2.4.14.4 Parallel diagnostic protocol processing
Multiple testers are a common scenario in today’s vehicles. In order to reduce the interference between concurrent tester requests to a minimum the Dcm supports parallel diagnostic service processing. This behavior is according to recommended practice of ISO 14229-1 Appendix J. There are certain restrictions, that in non-default session only diagnostic communication from one tester is allowed. In default session and for OBD-II communication it is possible to process diagnostic requests in parallel. Parallel OBD and UDS communication is particularly important if vehicles are equipped with so called ’OBD dongles’ or with electronical logging devices. These devices are installed by the vehicle owner and do diagnostic communication over standardized OBD services. The presence of such devices shall interfere as little as possible with vehicle internal UDS communication. Therefore, whenever it is possible, the Dcm supports parallel processing.

7.2.4.16.4 Diagnostic Activation State
The Dcm notifies the ComM module about the internal diagnostic state for all networks. There are two options for the diagnostic state on a network. In ’active’ diagnostic state, the Dcm is processing one or more diagnostic requests from this network or the Dcm is in a non-default session. In ’inactive’ diagnostic state, the Dcm is in default session and is not processing a diagnostic request on that network. When a network has no communication in progress, the Dcm will set the diagnostic activation state to ’inactive’. When there is a diagnostic communication on a network the Dcm sets the diagnostic state to ’active’. In any non-default session, the diagnostic state remains in state ’active’. The communication state can also be controlled by the API Xxx_SetActiveDiagnostic according to [SWS_Dcm_01070] and [SWS_Dcm_01071].

7.2.4 Coordination of nested sub-busses
To support the coordination of nested sub-busses the Nm-Coordinators need be configured to build up a coordination hierarchy. The top most NM Coordinator has only actively coordinated channels (NmActiveCoordinator == TRUE) per coordination cluster. This NM Coordinator has to initiate the coordinated shutdown for all other coordinators. An nested NM Coordinator receive his shutdown indication information from his passively configured channel (NmActiveCoordinator == FALSE) and provides this information to following NM Coordinators via his actively coordinated channels ( NmActiveCoordinator == TRUE). The Figure 7.2 will explain this as an example. Figure 7.2: Use Case Nested Gateways The exemplary topology shown in Figure 7.2 has the following coordination approach. GW 1 have configured the channel onto Network 1 and Network 2 as actively coordinating channels. Where GW 2 is configured with Network 2 connection as passively coordinated channel, but with actively coordinated channel on Network 3. GW 3 than needs to be configured on Network 3 as passively coordinated channel but as actively coordinated channel for his connection to the Network 4.

7.3.2 Coordinated wakeup
Depending on the configuration, ComM can start multiple networks based on the indication from one network. It is recommended to configure the ComM to automatically start all network of a NM Coordination Cluster if one of the networks indicates network start, but this is not always necessary. Since the wakeup of network is outside the scope of Nm, this is independent of if the NM Coordination functionality is used or not.

7.3 Diagnostic Service Dispatcher (DSD)

7.3 Wakeup and abortion of the coordinated shutdown
Nm is not responsible for normal wakeup of the node or the networks this will be done by the COM Manager (ComM).

7.4.1.1 Bus wake up inhibition
Information: Bus wake up inhibition in context of the ComM module means that the ComM module should take precautions against awaking other ECUs by starting the communication. Rationale: Awaking other ECUs by communication should be avoided because it is assumed that the ECU wakes up the bus because of an error (e.g. broken sensor). Use Case: An error was detected on signal path of an active wake up line and this non reliable wake-up-source should not be able to awake the whole system anymore. An SW-C that controls error-reactions could set the wake up inhibition-status of related communication channels that usually get communication-requests from SW-Cs as the consequence of this event. This corrupts the forwarding of communication system-wide, based on unreliable wake up events. Or in case of application-specific system control, there is an SW-C that should switch off forwarding system wide wakeup’s by communication under conditions like e.g. transport mode.

7.4.1.1 Manage communication inhibition
In principle the utilization of communication inhibition is manageable. The execution permission of communication inhibition functionality is controlled via an inhibition status field (bit field). Each bit represents one communication inhibition functionality. The value of the control bit classifies, if the corresponding communication inhibition has the permission to be executed. The inhibition status field is stored non-volatile to survive an ECU reset. ComM restores the inhibition status field at start-up, if the inhibition status field is available in a non-volatile memory. Otherwise ComM uses the configuration of ComMEcuGroupClassification as default. Note: The layout of the inhibition status field is defined in [SWS_ComM_00669]. The following parameters are relevant for communication inhibition and have a relationship to APIs:
• ComMNoCom: "request bit" of mode inhibition (limit to NoCom), can be controlled by ComM_LimitChannelToNoComMode and ComM_LimitECUToNoComMode, only if ComMEcuGroupClassification enables this functionality (see [ECUC_ComM_00563], [SWS_ComM_00163], [SWS_ComM_00124]).
• ComMNoWakeup: "request bit" of mode inhibition (wakeup inhibition), can be controlled by ComM_PreventWakeUp, only if ComMEcuGroupClassification enables this functionality (see [ECUC_ComM_00563], [SWS_ComM_00156]).
• ComMEcuGroupClassification: "mask bits" of mode inhibition behavior, can be controlled by ComM_SetECUGroupClassification, regardless of ComMNoCom and ComMNoWakeup values

7.4.4.14.4 Parallel diagnostic protocol processing
Multiple testers are a common scenario in today’s vehicles. In order to reduce the interference between concurrent tester requests to a minimum the Dcm supports parallel diagnostic service processing. This behavior is according to recommended practice of ISO 14229-1 Appendix J. There are certain restrictions, that in non-default session only diagnostic communication from one tester is allowed. In default session and for OBD-II communication it is possible to process diagnostic requests in parallel. Parallel Manager OBD and UDS communication is particularly important if vehicles are equipped with so called ’OBD dongles’ or with electronical logging devices. These devices are installed by the vehicle owner and do diagnostic communication over standardized OBD services. The presence of such devices shall interfere as little as possible with vehicle internal UDS communication. Therefore, whenever it is possible, the Dcm supports parallel processing.
[SWS_Dcm_01602] Processing of parallel requests in default session ⌈If the Dcm receives a request and no further protocol with a higher priority is currently in a non-default session, the Dcm shall accept the new incoming request and process it.⌋ (RS_Diag_04021)
[SWS_Dcm_01603] No parallel processing in non-default session ⌈If the Dcm receives a request and a further protocol with a higher priority is currently in a non-default session, the Dcm shall decline the new received request according to
[SWS_Dcm_00727].⌋(RS_Diag_04021) Some Dcm interfaces provide access to different diagnostic services, e.g. interface RoutineService for subfunctions Start, Stop and Request Result of a RoutineControl (0x31) or the interface DataServices for the Read and Write operations. On these interfaces only a single client shall access to the data at any point in time.
[SWS_Dcm_01604] Delay parallel processing on the same interface ⌈If the Dcm receives a request and the service processing of this request requires a call to the same interface that is currently processing another request, the Dcm shall delay the call to the interface until the running operation on that interface has finished.⌋(RS_Diag_04021) If the Dcm delays the service processing due to [SWS_Dcm_01604] the standard timing behavior with P2 and NRC 0x78 apply. 7.4.4 Synchronized PNC shutdown functionality
The synchronized PNC shutdown is a functionality which is a cooperation of ComM, Nm and <Bus>Nm to ensure a synchronized PNC shutdown at almost the same point in time across the whole PN topology. A synchronized PNC shutdown is handled by ECUs in role of a top-level PNC coordinator or intermediate PNC coordinator and where the PNC gateway is enabled. If ComM of an ECU in the role of a top-level PNC coordinator detects that a PNC is released, the ComM requests a synchronized PNC shutdown by calling Nm_RequestSynchronizedPncShutdown per ComMChannel and ComMPnc. The Nm module store all requests and handle them in the context of the Nm_Mainfunction. The Nm module indicate the affected <Bus>Nms regarding an activated PNC shutdown process. The <Bus>Nms call the Nm module to provide the aggregated requests for a synchronized PNC shutdown as PNC bit vector per given NM-channel. The <Bus>Nms use the provided PNC bit vector to assemble a NM-PDU as PN shutdown message and transmit this NM message on the according NM channel. If a PN shutdown message is received by an ECU in the role of an intermediate PNC coordinator, the <Bus>Nms extract the PNC bit vector from the received PN shutdown message and forward the information by calling the callback function Nm_ForwardSynchronizedPncShutdown. The Nm’s configuration contains parameters that regulate support of optional features found in the bus specific NMs. Since Nm is only a pass-through interface layer regarding features that are not used by the NM Coordinator functionality, enabling these in Nm’s configuration will in many cases only enable the pass-through of the controlling API functions and the callback indications from the bus specific layers. ⌈When an ECU Manager action causes the state of a wakeup source to change, the ECU Manager module shall issue a mode request to the BswM to change the wakeup source’s mode to the new the wakeup source state.⌋ For the communication of these wakeup source states the type EcuM_WakeupStatusType (see SWS_ECUM_04041) is used. When the ECU Manager module is in the UP phase, wakeup events do not usually trigger state changes. They trigger the end of the Halt and Poll Sub-Phases, however. The ECU Manager module then executes the WakeupRestart Sequence automatically and returns thereafter to the UP phase. It is up to the integrator to configure rules in the BswM so that the ECU reacts correctly to the wakeup events, as the reaction depends fully on the current ECU (not ECU Management) state. If the wakeup source is valid, the BswM returns the ECU to its RUN state. If all wakeup events have gone back to NONE or EXPIRED, the BswM prepares the BSW for SLEEP or OFF again and invokes EcuM_GoDownHaltPoll. Summarizing: every pending event is validated independently (if configured) and the EcuM publishes the result as a mode request to the BswM, which in turn can trigger state changes in the EcuM.

7.6.4 Activities in the WakeupValidation Sequence
Since wakeup events can be generated unintentionally (e.g. EVM spike on CAN line), it is necessary to validate wakeups before the ECU resumes full operation. The validation mechanism is the same for all wakeup sources. When a wakeup event occurs, the ECU is woken up from its SLEEP state and execution resumes within the MCU_SetMode service of the MCU driver 7 . When the WakeupRestart Sequence has finished, the ECU Manager module will have a list of pending wakeup events to be validated (see [SWS_EcuM_02539] ). The ECU Manager module then releases the BSW Scheduler and all BSW MainFunctions; most notably in this case, the EcuM Main Function can resume processing. Implementation hint: Since SchM will be running at the end of the StartPostOS and WakeupRestart sequences, there is the possibility that the EcuM_MainFunction will initiate validation for a source whose stack has not yet been initialized. The integrator should configure appropriate modes which indicate that the stack is not available and disable the EcuM_MainFunction accordingly (see [2] ). 7Actually, the first code to be executed may be an ISR, e.g. a wakeup ISR. However, this is specific to hardware and/or driver implementation.

[SWS_EthSM_00024] ⌈The EthSM shall implement for each configured network handle one network mode state machine (EthSM statemachine).⌋()
[SWS_EthSM_00203] ⌈The EthSM statemachine shall consist of 2 main states: ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION and ETHSM_NO_COMMUNICATION.⌋()
[SWS_EthSM_00204] ⌈The ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION shall have 3 sub-states: ETHSM_STATE_OFFLINE, ETHSM_STATE_WAIT_TRCVLINK and ETHSM_ STATE_WAIT_ONLINE.⌋()
[SWS_EthSM_00205] ⌈The ETHSM_NO_COMMUNICATION shall have 3 sub-states: ETHSM_STATE_ONLINE, ETHSM_STATE_ONHOLD and ETHSM_STATE_WAIT_ OFFLINE.⌋() The following points give an overview, on how the EthSM statemachine generally reacts on requested communication modes:
1. If communication mode COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION is requested for a certain Ethernet network and the corresponding EthSM statemachine is in state ETHSM_NO_COMMUNICATION, then at least the following preconditions have to be fulfilled to transit to ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION:
• Request ETH_MODE_ACTIVE for the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller.
• The corresponding Ethernet hardware has indicated ETHTRCV_LINK_ STATE_ACTIVE (active link state, thus, Ethernet cable is connected) via Eth SM_TrcvLinkStateChg
• The corresponding TcpIpCtrl has indicated TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE (IP communication is available) via EthSM_TcpIpModeIndication
2. If communication mode COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION_WITH_WAKEUP_ REQUEST is requested for a certain Ethernet network, EthSMWakeupSleepOn DatalineEnabled is set to TRUE and the corresponding EthSM statemachine is in state ETHSM_NO_COMMUNICATION, then at least the following preconditions have to be fulfilled to transit to ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION:
• Request ETH_MODE_ACTIVE_WITH_WAKEUP_REQUEST for the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller.
• The corresponding Ethernet hardware has indicated ETHTRCV_LINK_ STATE_ACTIVE (active link state, thus, Ethernet cable is connected) via Eth SM_TrcvLinkStateChg
• The corresponding TcpIpCtrl has indicated TCPIP_STATE_ONLINE (IP communication is available) via EthSM_TcpIpModeIndication
3. If ComM request COMM_SILENT_COMMUNICATION and the corresponding EthSM state machine is in state ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION, then the following actions will be performed:
• EthSM request ETH_MODE_ACTIVE_TX_OFFLINE for the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller, if forwarding of silent communication is enabled (see [ECUC_EthSM_00110])
• EthSM state machine transit to ETHSM_STATE_WAIT_OFFLINE
4. If the ComM requests COMM_NO_COMMUNICATION and the corresponding EthSM state machine is in state ETHSM_STATE_WAIT_OFFLINE, then the following preconditions have to be fulfilled to transist to ETHSM_NO_COMMUNICATION:
• EthSM request ETH_MODE_DOWN for the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller
• The corresponding TcpIpCtrl has indicated TCPIP_STATE_OFFLINE
5. If communication mode COMM_FULL_COMMUNICATION_WITH_WAKEUP_ REQUEST is requested for a certain Ethernet network, EthSMWakeupSleepOn DatalineEnabled is set to TRUE and the corresponding EthSM statemachine is in state ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION, then the EthSM request ETH_MODE_ ACTIVE_WITH_WAKEUP_REQUEST for the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller, even though the current state is ETHSM_FULL_COMMUNICATION The call of silent communication in point 3 will disable the transmission path of the corresponding Ethernet Interface Controller, if the forwarding of the request is configured (see [ECUC_EthSM_00110]) The re-trigger of the Ethernet Interface Controller described in point 5 in the previous section is used to request the lower layer to trigger a wake-up on the network. 7.6 UP Phase
In the UP Phase, the EcuM_MainFunction is executed regularly and it has three major functions:
• To check if wakeup sources have woken up and to initiate wakeup validation, if necessary (see 7.6.4 Activities in the WakeupValidation Sequence)
• To update the Alarm Clock timer
• Arbitrate RUN and POST_RUN requests and releases.

<Bus>Nm, then ComM is immediately indicated via ComM_Nm_ForwardSynchronizedPnc

8.5 Callout Definitions
Callouts are code fragments that must be added to the ECU Manager module during ECU integration. The content of most callouts is hand-written code. The ECU Manager module configuration tool generates a default implementation for some callouts which is edited manually by the integrator. Conceptually, these callouts belong to the ECU integration code.

8.5 Scheduled functions
These functions are directly called by Basic Software Scheduler. The following functions shall have no return value and no parameter. All functions shall be non reentrant.

8.6.1.1 Remark: Usage of CanIf_SetPduMode
Although the CanIf module provides more requestable PDU modes, the CanSM module only uses the parameters CANIF_ONLINE, CANIF_TX_OFFLINE_ACTIVE and CANIF_TX_OFFLINE for the call of the API CanIf_SetPduMode. The CANIF_OFFLINE mode is assumed automatically by CanIf and needs not to be set by CanSM.

operation between the parameter DTCStatusMask
and the current UDS status in the server. In addition
to the DTCStatusAvailabilityMask, the server shall
return all DTCs for which the result of the AND-ing
operation is non-zero [i.e. (statusOfDTC &
DTCStatusMask) != 0]. The server shall process
only the DTC Status bits that it is supporting. OBD
Events Suppression shall be ignored for this
computation. If no DTCs within the server match the
masking criteria specified in the client’s request, no
DTC or status information shall be provided
following the DTCStatusAvailabilityMask byte in the
positive response message

This chapter will show use-cases for LIN communication and API usage. As the communication is in real-time it is not easy to show the real-time behavior in the UML dynamic diagrams. It is advisable to read the corresponding descriptive text to each UML diagram. To show the behavior of the modules in the different use-cases, there are local function calls made to show what is done and when to get information. It is not mandatory to use these local functions; they are here just to make the use-cases more understandable. Note that all parameters and return types are left out to make the diagrams easier to read and understand. If needed for clarification the parameter value or return value are shown.

The LSduR_ IEEE1722TpTransmit is called. The L-SDU Router module will convert the source L-SDU ID (L-SDU Router module configuration) to one L-SDU ID for EthIf (EthIf module configuration). The PduInfoType value received from the IEEE1722Tp module is copied to the EthIf module without change. Example: The EthIf module will call LSduR_EthIfTxConfirmation with an L-SDU ID and, dependent on the success of the transmission, with a result E_OK (successful transmission) or E_NOT_OK (not successful transmission). Then the L-SDU Router module will convert this L-SDU ID and forward the call to IEEE1722Tp

Figure 7.1: I-PDU ID Example [SWS_PduR_00161] Upstream requirements: SRS_GTW_06003 ⌈The PDU Router module shall identify a routing path uniquely by the combination of source module I-PDU ID (located in the PDU Router configuration) and destination I-PDU IDs (located in the called destination module configurations). ⌋ [SWS_PduR_00766] Upstream requirements: SRS_GTW_06003 ⌈The PDU Router module shall convert the I-PDU ID to the destination module(s) for both Transmit path and TxConfirmation/RxIndication path.⌋ Example: The Com module transmits an I-PDU to CanIf and LinIf. The PduR_Com Transmit is called. The PDU Router module will convert the source I-PDU ID (PDU Router module configuration) to one I-PDU ID for LinIf (LinIf module configuration) and one I-PDU ID for CanIf (CanIf module configuration). The PduInfoType value received from the Com module is copied to the CanIf and LinIf modules without change. Example: The LinIf will call PduR_LinIfTxConfirmation with an I-PDU ID and, dependent on the success of the transmission, with a result E_OK (successful transmission) or E_NOT_OK (not successful transmission). Then the PDU Router module will convert this I-PDU ID and forward the call to Com using Com_TxConfirmation with the converted I-PDU ID and the received result.

11.5 Post-build considerations
This section describes some important behavior when using the post-build variant of the PDU Router. It contains no requirements, just important issues that need to be considered. NVRAM and RAM memory size can potentially grow if a new post-build configuration is downloaded into the ECU. Estimation at design time must be done to allow such grow so other areas are not overwritten (in case of RAM) or memory borders are not crossed. It is not possible to configure restrictions/locations/etc of memory in the PduR module configuration since this is implementation specific and relitevly difficult to implement (pre-compile and link-time does not really need this). It is recommended for implementations of PduR module generators to extend the configuration with specific memory constraints if needed. A Not applicable requirements

2.4.4 API Function Parameters [TR_BSWMG_00020] API Function Parameters ⌈The function parameters shall have mandatory entries for “Name”, “Type”, “Direction” and “Notes”.⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00032] API Function Parameter types ⌈The parameter “Type” shall be one of the existing types defined in the BSW model.⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00033] C-Style Pointers as API Function Parameters ⌈Parameters may be modeled as C-Style pointers by appending * to the parameter type, e.g. PduInfoType*⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00027] Mandatory pointers for API Function Output Parameters ⌈Parameters must be modeled as pointers if their “Direction” attribute is set to out or inout.⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00035] Mandatory constant types for pointers of API Function Input Parameters ⌈Pointer-type parameters of direction type “in", i.e. parameters that represent read-only structures or arrays, may prepend the parameter type with the const keyword. This enforces that the data pointed to by the parameter is read-only and will not be altered by the function. Example: const FrIf_ConfigType*⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00021] API Function Parameter Direction ⌈The parameter’s direction type attribute shall be set to one of the values in, out, inout, return.⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00022] API Function Parameter Description ⌈Each parameter shall provide a short description about its purpose.⌋() Note: EA provides a textfield called ‘Notes’ to take the parameters description. [TR_BSWMG_00023] API Function Return Parameter ⌈If the function’s return type is not equal to void, the return value shall be modeled like an operation parameter with the following exceptions: It shall be the first parameter in the list. Additionally, it shall be the only parameter to have its “Direction” set to “return”. The notes field shall concisely describe the possible return values.⌋() Modeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML Model Figure 2.5: Parameter example of a API function [TR_BSWMG_00922] API Function Return Value Links ⌈All possible return values for an API function’s return parameter that are described in the notes field of the parameter shall be linked to the definition of the value. In particular, if the function’s return type is a simple type (see [TR_BSWMG_00066]) the link shall be put as [ARDataTypeElement{}{}]. If it is an enumeration (see [TR_BSWMG_00072]) the link shall be put as [AREnumLiteral{}{}]. Note that shall be set to the anchor name (see [TR_BSWMG_00031]) of the datatype if one is defined.⌋() Example: The correct way to link the return values in the example of Figure 2.5 is to put this description into the notes field of the return parameter: [ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was successful
[ARDataTypeElement{E_NOT_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: Cancellation of request timeout was not successful Note: If the return type has an extension (as defined in 2.4.8.3) then always the type in the model defining the current value has to be linked. Example: If an API function in the Csm module returns the Std_ReturnType then e.g. values E_OK and CRYPTO_E_BUSY may be returned as the latter value is defined in Csm_ReturnType, which is an extension to Std_ReturnType. In that case the links have to be set like this: [ARDataTypeElement{E_OK}{Std_ReturnType}]: ...
[ARDataTypeElement{CRYPTO_E_BUSY}{Csm_ReturnType}]: ... Modeling Guidelines of Basic Software EA UML Model [TR_BSWMG_00129] Optional Parameters of API Functions ⌈The existence of a parameter may depend on the module configuration. In this case, the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪optional≫.⌋() [TR_BSWMG_00130] Multiplicity of API Function Parameters ⌈A parameter with a given type may occur several times, where the multiplicity is specified by configuration. In this case, the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪multiple≫.⌋() Hint: Don’t use the multiplicity button in the parameter edit mask to configure the multiplicity. [TR_BSWMG_00131] Mutual Exclusive Variants of API Function Parameters ⌈A parameter may appear in different variants within the same position of the function signature, where one specific variant will be selected by configuration. In this case, the parameter shall be modeled several times in all its possible variants and each variant of the parameter shall have the stereotype ≪mutualexcl≫.⌋() Example: The parameter “buffer” of the Xfrm function “_” can be configured either as “inout” or “out”. It therefore shall be modeled two times, one time with Direction “inout” and the second time with Direction “out”. Since Enterprise Architect requires parameter names to be unique, the first parameter variant may be named “buffer{inout}” and the second one “buffer{out}”. Hint: All variants of a mutual exclusive parameter shall have the same name; the name without the curly brackets (including the text) have to be the same. In order to support the synchronization of Handle IDs (see section 3.4.1) two modules
need to be able to refer to the same Pdu object2. Therefore a generic Pdu container
has been defined which does not belong to any module but is defined in the EcuC
module.

N-PDU.

module is used to collect configuration information not associated with any specific

The EcucPduCollection may contain several "global" Pdu objects as shown in figure 3.9. Each Pdu may either represent a FrameTriggering (for Pdus not going
through the Pdu Router: UserDefinedPdus, NmPdus and NPdus) or PduTriggering (for all other Pdus) belonging to the specific ECU from the AUTOSAR System
Description[1] (ECU Extract).
Therefore there is an optional reference to either FrameTriggering (SysTPduToFrameTriggeringRef) or PduTriggering
(SysTPduToPduTriggeringRef) element in the System Template. Either SysTPduToFrameTriggeringRef or SysTPduToPduTriggeringRef shall be used.

7.1.3.2.2 Error handling
For errors occurred using singlecast or multicast over Communication Interface modules, no specific error handling is done. Errors in return values are forwarded to the upper layer source module.

7.1.3.3.1 Multicast transmission
This subsection contains specific requirements for the multicast transmission of I-PDU using Transport Protocol modules. Since the 1:n, n>1 routing is made in the PDU Router module the PDU Router module must request the same data several times from the upper layer source module. Also the confirmation of the multicast must be handled specifically. As the upper layer shall copy the same data several times, the PDU Router will use the RetryInfoPtr [7] in order to query the same data several times. The RetryInfo Ptr contains a state type called TpDataState . Therefore the transport protocol destinations do not set the TpDataState to TP_ DATARETRY.
[SWS_PduR_00871] ⌈When PduR_<User:LoTp>CopyTxData is called with a Tp DataState set to TP_DATARETRY for a multicast TP transmission type routing path, PduR shall return E_NOT_OK.⌋() The multicast transmission of N-PDUs is performed in a lock-step mode, where the slowest destination dictates the rate of transmission. The use-case behind the multicast multiframe transmission is the broadcast of J1939Tp BAM messages (messages like DM1 or CommandedAddress have more than 8 Bytes and need to be broadcast to several destinations).
[SWS_PduR_00872] ⌈When PduR_<User:LoTp>CopyTxDatais called for a multicast TP transmission session for a destination which previously had already fetched more data than the upper layer buffer’s read index currently points to, PduR shall return BUFREQ_E_BUSY.⌋() Implementation hint: In this case for each destination PduR must remember how many bytes have been transmitted so far and also shall keep tracking.
[SWS_PduR_00631] ⌈For a new multicast TP transmission session, the request of PduR_<User:LoTp>CopyTxData of the first destination shall be forwarded with Tp DataState set to TP_CONFPENDING.⌋(SRS_GTW_06029)
[SWS_PduR_00632] ⌈For all subsequential calls of PduR_<User:LoTp>CopyTxData for the same multicast TP transmission session, PduR shall overwrite TpData State to TP_DATARETRY and adjust Tx TpData Cnt to request data to be transmitted from the upper layer source buffer from the previous transmission point related to that destination.⌋(SRS_GTW_06029) Note: Tx TpData Cnt is an "Offset from the current position." see Specification of Communication Stack Types [7].
[SWS_PduR_00812] ⌈After all Transport Protocols have received their data the PDU Router module may confirm the data to the upper layer module.⌋(SRS_GTW_- 06029)
[SWS_PduR_00765] ⌈In case of multicast transmission, the PDU Router module shall call the upper layer module using <Up>_TpTxConfirmation after receiving the last PduR_<User:LoTp>TxConfirmation from the lower layer Transport Protocol modules. 7.1.3.3.2 Error handling
The PDU Router module will not take specific actions on errors occurred, the errors will be forwarded to the upper layer source module via return value. Appropriate error handling is in the responsibility of the upper layer module.

7.1.4.3 Forwarding to upper layers
If the I-PDU is gatewayed (direct Transport Protocol gateway) to one or more destinations of transport protocol module(s), this I-PDU may be also received by a local upper layer module. However combined forwarding and gatewaying in n:1 fashion is not supported. In case of multiple Software Clusters, this I-PDU may also be received by several upper layer modules. As the relevance of such scenario is limited to functional addressing of multiple Dcm instances in a clusters software architecture, the constraint to support it for direct gatewaying only, does not pose a problem because only I-PDUs of limited size can be expected. Implementations may choose to report (via DET) whenever the upper layer reception was not successful. The gatewaying to lower layers should not be aborted in this case. The reception to the upper layers of direct gatewaying is specified below:
[SWS_PduR_00789] Upstream requirements: SRS_GTW_06026, SRS_GTW_06029
⌈In case of gatewaying, when a successful RxIndication is received by PduR from the lower layer, the module shall initiate a reception session for a configured upper layer destination: <UpTp>_StartOfReception, <UpTp>_CopyRxData, and <UpTp>_Rx Indication will be called in this order.⌋

7.4.11.3 Buffer Locking
At the sender side, the originator of the transmission (e.g. DCM or COM) shall not change the buffer after a successful Transmit call until the connection is closed by a call to TxConfirmation. When a cyclic buffer is used, the data in this buffer must be kept until it is explicitly freed by PduR_FrArTpCopyTxData with retry.TpDataState set to TP_DATACONF. At the receiver side, the module that provides the receive buffer (e.g. DCM or COM) shall not change this buffer after a successful call to StartOfReception until the connection is closed by a call to PduR_FrArTpRxIndication. When a cyclic buffer is used, Layer it may assume that all data provided via PduR_FrArTpCopyRxData is valid and may be discarded immediately.

7.4.2 Scheduling of PDUs during Transmission
PDUs of a PDU pool must be assigned to all active connections in a way that no connection freezes, while connections with prioritized PDUs are served first.
[SWS_FrArTp_00256] ⌈To achieve an even distribution of PDUs to all currently transmitting and/or receiving connections associated with a PDU pool, the PDUs of this pool shall be assigned to active connections using round robin scheduling. A connection that is currently receiving and transmitting may claim two PDUs in one round of the assignment: one for the FC, and one for an SF/FF/CF.⌋
[SWS_FrArTp_00257] ⌈The scheduling shall be executed in the context of the main function, and shall start with the connection where the scheduling stopped in the previous cycle.⌋
[SWS_FrArTp_00258] ⌈Each PDU assignment cycle shall start with the prioritized PDUs. In this phase, PDUs are only assigned to active connections with prioritized PDUs, until their needs are satisfied. Afterwards, PDU assignment continues for all active connections.⌋

7.4 Meta Data Handling
Meta data of PDUs is supported by a large number of modules of the communication stack. It serves to transport information through the layers, that is in general abstracted by the layered architecture. The first supported meta data was the CAN ID of PDUs related to CanIf. The meta data is transported by the PduInfoType structure via a separate pointer to a byte array alongside the length of and a pointer to the payload of the PDU. 7.5 Best Match Algorithm
[SWS_SoAd_00680] ⌈SoAd shall use the following best match algorithm to select a socket connection of a socket connection group based on a provided (specific) remote address:
1. socket connections that have no (specific or wildcard) remote address set shall be ignored
2. the remote address of the remaining socket connections shall be compared with the provided remote address and the socket connection with the best match according to the following ordered list (item listed earlier has higher priority towards items listed later) shall be selected:
(a) IP address and port match
(b) IP address match (and wildcard set for port)
(c) Port match (and wildcard set for IP address)
(d) Wildcards are used for both IP address and port

7.6 Gateway functionality
The SecOC module supports authentication and verification for I-PDUs that are routed from one source bus to one or more destination busses. This allows for the realization of re-authentication gateways that can be used to realize networks with different security zones or properties. The actions necessary to support the required gateway functionality can be simply derived from the authentication and verification scenarios in Sections 7.4 and 7.5. Each authentication or verification process for a given I-PDU need to be configured separately. This functionality includes:
 authentication of outgoing I-PDUs,
 verification of incoming I-PDUs,
 re-authentication gateways, i.e. the verification of incoming I-PDUs in combination of their immediate re-authentication, when the I-PDU is routed to another lower layer module. Note: “Gatewaying-on-the-fly” is not supported by SecOC

BufReq_ReturnType

completely as requested.

current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to

)
Service ID [hex]
0x3e
Sync/Async
Synchronous
Reentrancy
Non Reentrant for same ComUserCbkHandleId, otherwise Reentrant
ComUserCbkHandleId
Com user callback handle Id corresponding to the transmitted
I-PDU.
info
Provides the destination buffer (SduDataPtr) and the number of
bytes to be copied (SduLength). If not enough transmit data is
available, no data is copied by the upper layer module and
BUFREQ_E_BUSY is returned. The lower layer module may
retry the call. An SduLength of 0 can be used to indicate state
changes in the retry parameter or to query the current amount of
available data in the upper layer module. In this case, the Sdu
DataPtr may be a NULL_PTR.
Parameters (in)
retry
Will not be handled by Com and its upper layer.
Parameters (inout)
None
Parameters (out)
availableDataPtr
Indicates the remaining number of bytes that are available in the
upper layer module’s Tx buffer. availableDataPtr can be used by
TP modules that support dynamic payload lengths (e.g. FrIsoTp)
to determine the size of the following CFs.
Return value
BufReq_ReturnType
BUFREQ_OK: Data has been copied to the transmit buffer
completely as requested.
BUFREQ_E_BUSY: Request could not be fulfilled, because the
required amount of Tx data is not available. The lower layer
module may retry this call later on. No data has been copied.
BUFREQ_E_NOT_OK: Data has not been copied. Request
failed.
Description
This function is called to acquire the transmit data of an I-PDU segment (N-PDU). Each call to
this function provides the next part of the I-PDU data unless retry->TpDataState is TP_
DATARETRY. In this case the function restarts to copy the data beginning at the offset from the
current position indicated by retry->TxTpDataCnt. The size of the remaining data is written to
the position indicated by availableDataPtr
